_what: What curation/dahlmanje_30394729 (Sago 2018, PMID 30394729) shares with the live corpus. Produced by 02_corpus_overlap.py.

token_pattern_test.verdict: A substring join on the bare token '7C1' captures 36 corpus rows spanning 35 distinct structures across 4 experiments, and NOT ONE of them is Dahlman's 7C1 lipomer: they are combinatorial labels in which the characters happen to co-occur (KL_2010 '117C14' = head 117 + C14; LL_2012 'A7C10'; LM_2019 'A1Iso7C11'; ZH_2023 'A4I18R7C18-2'). The paper's own '7C1' is a compound index from Dahlman 2014, not a composition: the '7' is the amine and the 'C1' is the epoxide index, while the drawn tail is C13 and the epoxide is C15. Three different numbers, none of them a chain length.

substructure_sweep_SUPERSET._what: SUPERSET, not an identification. The loose pattern is 'any amine bearing CH2-CH(OH)-CH2', the amino-alcohol motif an epoxide ring-opening leaves; it matches a whole chemotype and says nothing about 7C1. The strict pattern additionally requires the full 13-carbon tail the paper draws. Neither can identify 7C1, because 7C1 is a polydisperse polymer with no single SMILES: a strict hit would be a small molecule carrying the same arm, not this lipid.

peg_lipid_names.note: The paper names no catalogue product. Fig 3B draws a diacyl glycerophosphoethanolamine-PEG, which for C14/C16/C18 would be DMPE-/DPPE-/DSPE-PEG2000 -- two of those three names already exist in the corpus. The mapping is an INFERENCE from a drawn skeleton, so it is recorded and not applied; and PEG-lipids are deliberately absent from provenance/reagent_registry.py anyway, because the block length is a distribution.

in_vivo_shared_chemistry.why: This paper's only ionizable lipid is 7C1, which has no SMILES and is absent from the corpus under any name. It adds no shared in-vivo chemistry. It also uses no benchmark ionizable lipid at all -- no MC3, no SM-102, no ALC-0315 anywhere in the paper; its only comparator is its own 80:20 7C1 formulation.
